newsitem.title: MEXICO: Hylsamex sees 10 pct sales growth in '97.
newsitem.headline: Hylsamex sees 10 pct sales growth in '97.

text.p: Mexican steelmaker Hylsamex sees sales increases of about 10 percent in volume and dollar terms this year, its chief financial officer said on Friday.
"Growth in sales should be around 10 percent as we are expecting prices to more or less hold steady in dollar terms during the year," said Ernesto Ortiz.
Hylsamex notched up total sales of $1.151 billion in 1996.
"We assume shipments should grow by around 10 percent. In 1996, they totalled 12.4 million tonnes," Ortiz added, while speaking at a meeting with analysts.
Ortiz said he saw cash flow in 1997 increasing by some 12 percent from the $287 million posted in 1996.
Hylsamex is also negotiating a credit line for $80 million with export contracts as collateral, he said.
"We should have it available at the beginning of next month. The manager is Santander, with a six-month maturity plus one month's grace and at a rate of Libor plus 150 basis points," Ortiz said.

In addition, Hylsamex is seeking loans of $115 million from Eximbanks in the United States, Canada, Germany and Italy which, together with the $80 million credit line and in-house resources, will fund investment programs totaling $370 million for 1997 and 1998.
